reason: While the text describes severe suffering (siege, famine, destruction of Jerusalem, exile) and contains theological interpretation that this suffering resulted from wrongdoing (Zedekiah 'did evil in the sight of the Lord' and it came 'because of the anger of the Lord'), the passage does not show leaders directly telling the people that their suffering is their fault. When Gedaliah, the appointed governor, addresses the people, he instructs them to 'fear not the servants of the Chaldeans' and to 'serve the king of Babylon' for their own benefit—not to blame themselves for their suffering.
